handled_verified.note: Z14 (deep review, 2026-09-28): `opaque_declaration` joins this list as a CONTAINER — `opaque {}` declares no fields but does declare functions and constants, and 123 opaque containers / 352 declarations in the pinned corpora were published with no owner, no `scope` and no `contains` edge before the fix (Z12). `function_signature` is the ANONYMOUS fn-type form (`f: *const fn (u8) void` — 960 in the corpora); it is reached by the walk and mints no symbol because an fn type has no name identifier, which supersedes ZIGD2's claim below that no valid Zig source produces it. `test_declaration`/`comptime_declaration` are executable SCOPE (no declaration symbols), not declaration sites. `block` is listed because it is the structural executable-body marker (Z19). Z50: `ERROR` and `MISSING` are the universal tree-sitter pair that F1, the bash F8 census and the completeness inventory all require to be classified (completeness-inventory.ts:832-840 adds them to every language's enumeration because the wasm ABI's nodeTypeForId does not list them). Zig was the lane failing section A on this pair while HANDLING both explicitly at real-zig-analyzer.ts:736 (`node.type === "ERROR" || node.isMissing`), which pushes a diagnostic per occurrence with 1-based columns (Z2) and deliberately does NOT use `node.hasError`, because the root spans the whole file and one parse error would then cascade into 163 pipeline rows on aro/Attribute.zig (#897). Classified handled_verified because consulting the node and reporting it once per occurrence is handling. The alternative - leaving the pair unclassified and calling the gate's enumeration drift - is what that comment explicitly warns against.

gap._description: Zig declaration surface modeled from the pinned tree-sitter-zig AST, re-measured 2026-09-28 over THREE corpora (zig 2,950 + zls 90 + ghostty 799 = 3,839 .zig files; 92 named node types, 140 anonymous token types, 16 field names). Prior ZGD-wave (M37 #600, 2026-09-04) rulings stand: ZGD1 write gate (AMENDED by Z15 — the gate tests the OPERATOR, so a compound assignment is a read-modify-write), ZGD2 bare/qualified return-type refs, ZGD3 executable scope (AMENDED by Z19 — the rule belongs on the `block`, which covers labeled blocks the two wrapper node types missed), ZGD4 usingnamespace imports, ZGD5/5b enum-literal and type-position uses suppression. Z14 wave: Z11 kind dispatch, Z12 opaque containers, Z13 declared-type leaf from the `type` field, Z14 the references oracle, Z15 compound assignment, Z16 the local annotation position, Z17 dead code, Z17b/Z17c declared-type payloads, Z18 the last regex, Z19 the executable body, Z20 export members. M12 ground truth (validation/m12/ground-truth/zig.json) is SYMBOLS-ONLY and predates the calls/uses contract; it is not contradicted by this wave, and the symbol facts it records still hold.

gaps.missing: CORRECTED. The gap used to read "`opaque {}` types parse cleanly but emit no symbol ... the type is intentionally not indexed", which was false on both halves: the analyzer emitted a `Type` symbol for every opaque, and it emitted the WRONG ones for what the type declares. An opaque type is now a container (Z12): 123 opaque containers and 352 declarations in the pinned corpora are owned, with `contains` edges, and their `pub fn` members are Methods.

`test "name" {}` blocks emit no function symbol (anonymous, unstable scope). Calls and field-uses inside a test body are still captured with source '(global)', so the code-intel graph does not lose them.

gaps.severity: partially closed by Z32; the remainder is measured
gaps.missing: A type used in a VALUE position with no type annotation — `const p = Point{ .x = 1 };` — published no edge. Z32 closed the in-file half by publishing it as `instantiates` with `isConstructorApplication`, which is exactly the family alternative this gap named (`instantiates` with `isConstructor`, as c/cpp emit). REMAINDER, measured over 400 corpus files: an in-file inventory cannot resolve a QUALIFIED callee, and there are 19,318 call sites whose callee is a field_expression (`std.ArrayList(u8)`, `self.allocator.alloc(...)`) plus 381 whose callee is an identifier that is not a symbol in this file at all. Classifying those needs a CROSS-FILE type index — a different instrument, not a fix in this one — so the gap is stated as the population it is, and the number moves only if that index is built.

Three RHS forms stay on the upper-case-name heuristic because the grammar cannot separate a type from a value without resolution: `const X = (SomeType)` (parenthesized), `const X = SomeStruct{ ... }` (a struct initializer) and `const X = someGeneric(u8)` (a call-shaped type application). MEASURED rather than assumed (script/m14/tmp/zigw-gap4.ts, 1,200 corpus files): of the 8,240 sites that ride the heuristic, the file can resolve only 2,951, and of those 29 (1.0%) disagree with the published kind - and every disagreement examined is a bug in the PROBE's resolver, not in the analyzer (Zig's generic type FUNCTIONS - `const Fixed = FixedPoint(i32, 16, 16)` where `fn FixedPoint(comptime T: type, ...)` yields a TYPE; `[_]struct { ... }` is an array of values, not a type). The other 5,289 sites are external names the file cannot speak about at all (@import aliases, `std.Build.Step.Run`), which no in-file resolution pass could ever reach. CONCLUSION: a per-file type-resolution pass is not worth building - the heuristic is not measurably wrong anywhere a file can resolve, and the population it would have to guess about is 64% unresolvable in principle. The limitation stands as a ruling, and the first version of the probe (which reported 64.6% wrong) is recorded here as the reason to calibrate a measurement before believing it.

The grammar has ONE node type for Zig's labeled block (`V = blk: { … break :blk v; }`) and its labeled type (`T = L: u32 { … return v; }`), and the TYPE form does not parse: probed as an ERROR node on the `u32`. All 9 corpus instances of the node are labeled blocks. The kind dispatch therefore reads the shape (breaks, never returns) rather than the node type, which is a rule with one measured outcome and a documented grammar limit rather than a grammar fact it cannot rely on.

decisions.question: Zig has no class inheritance, no interfaces with implements clauses, no overrides, and no implicit type instantiation the way C++/Java do — how are these relationship kinds handled?
decisions.resolution: By design, Zig emits NO extends/implements/overrides/instantiates edges. Composition is expressed through struct fields and opaque vtables; generics are compile-time monomorphized without a runtime type dispatch the analyzer can attribute statically. requiredKinds for zig reflect only the emitted kinds: calls, uses, contains, references.

decisions.question: Zig evaluates top-level `const`, `comptime`, and `test` block initializers at compile time — these are call sites outside any function body.
decisions.resolution: Field-accesses and calls in any non-function context (top-level const initializers, comptime blocks, test bodies) emit with source '(global)', mirroring the go family package-scope-call contract. Without this, fmt.zig's `const assert = std.debug.assert;` (a real dependency) would be silently dropped — measured 745 edges were lost before this fix (zig wave 2026-08-29).

decisions.question: Error-set members (`error{ A, B }`) are identifiers, and @-prefixed builtins are intrinsics, not user symbols.
decisions.resolution: An identifier whose parent is error_set_declaration is emitted as an EnumMember (members cannot collide with the declaring variable's LHS). @builtin_function callees (@import/@intCast/@as) are compile-time intrinsics and emit NO calls edge — they are never user symbols.

decisions.question: Is function_signature a real, fixture-coverable shape in the pinned grammar? The original ruling said NO valid Zig source produces it.
decisions.resolution: CORRECTION (Z14/Z17 wave, 2026-09-28): the original claim was FALSE against this grammar. A corpus census over 3,839 files found 960 function_signature nodes, all of them the ANONYMOUS fn-type form: `f: *const fn (u8) void` inside a container field, and `const Cb = fn (x: u32) void;` as a declaration RHS (8 upper-case sites). The CONCLUSION is unchanged and now rests on a grammar fact instead of a negative: an fn type has no name identifier, so the walk's name test finds nothing and mints no symbol. The negative claim was the kind of assertion nothing checks — a future grammar could have satisfied it without anyone noticing, and in the meantime it justified a `function_signature` branch in a code path no reviewer could confirm was reachable.

decisions.question: test/comptime blocks contain block bodies — are their locals declaration symbols?
decisions.resolution: ZGD3: NO — the walk previously fell through with inFunction=false and every test body leaked file-scope Variable symbols (violating the analyzer's own execution-artifact contract). Both blocks now set the executable-scope flag; their call/use edges still emit with source '(global)' per ZIG.D.2.

decisions.question: Is `usingnamespace @import("x.zig");` an import fact?
decisions.resolution: ZGD4: YES — first-class import (imports array + references edge, meta.usingnamespace). The walk previously dropped these declarations entirely. Process lesson recorded: an earlier fix draft targeted an assignment-RHS usingnamespace form that is NOT valid Zig (grammar error-recovers it into call_expression + ERROR child); the pinned grammar + probe exposed the invented form before it shipped. Fixture authored from the probed declaration shape.

decisions.question: Zig review (2026-09-12): every symbol reported the synthetic complexity 3 regardless of body — the removed-everywhere-else disease was still live in zig.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: per-symbol complexity is the real zigBodyComplexity (if/for/while/switch/catch/else + and/or/orelse operator tokens). Fixture zig/bare-value-reads pins score=5, guard=4; mutants zig/synthetic-complexity and zig/drop-symbol-complexity CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Zig review (2026-09-12): parse-error ranges carried raw 0-based startColumn/endColumn (the svelte-wave class) while every other zig range is 1-based.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: errors now 1-based like nodeRange. Fixture zig/bare-value-reads pins the stray-brace error at line 103 column 1; mutant zig/error-columns-0based CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Zig review (2026-09-12): `return Limit` / `return counter` emitted NOTHING — the analyzer and the differential oracle were BOTH blind to bare identifier reads of file-scope values.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: analyzeZigBareIdentifierUses walks with walk-order lexical scopes (params, blocks, payload captures, var/const bindings only — C6: assignments write, never bind); resolves only file-scope Constant/Variable/Function/EnumMember names; suppresses defining positions, callees, member leaves, labels, blanks, shadowed names. Fixture zig/bare-value-reads pins the positive surface; mutants zig/drop-bare-uses and zig/reemit-shadowed-reads CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Zig review (2026-09-12): two error-member defects — (a) declaration sites read themselves (`pub const Error = error{ WriteFailed, OutOfMemory };` emitted uses WriteFailed at its own declaration; probe-verified on zls src/print_zoir.zig), and (b) the analyzer resolved EVERY enum member by name globally while the oracle only resolved value-position error leaves (`return error.Timeout`), so payload binding names and struct type positions collided with enum members on zls.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: error_set_declaration direct identifiers are defining occurrences; enum members resolve ONLY as value-position error-type leaves (parameter/field/container_field error types are declared-type facts, never reads). Fixture zig/bare-value-reads (expects fail->Timeout, handle->Fatal; forbids Unused/Widget/identifier_usage->fast); mutants zig/reemit-error-set-declaration, zig/drop-error-member-uses, zig/global-enum-member-uses CAUGHT. Lane differential zig:zig and zig:zls both 0 missing / 0 unexplained.

decisions.question: Zig review (2026-09-12): the Z3 oracle re-derived its own name table (owner-blind pre-pass, kind-dispatch order, container attribution) and diverged from the analyzer by 70+ phantom MISSING edges across the upstream zig corpus.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: deriveZigBareUses takes the analyzer's OWN symbols as its name inventory (file-scope kinds + global EnumMember set); truth still derives every EDGE independently from tree structure — only the inventory is shared ground truth, exactly like the grammar. Lane replica script/m14/tmp/zig-lane-pairs.ts: zig 0/0, zls 0/0.

decisions.question: Extreme review (2026-09-12): switch-arm captures bound into the enclosing block/function frame (and file-scope switches had no frame at all) — a global capture name emitted a junk bare read, and an arm capture leaked past its arm and swallowed a post-switch genuine read of a same-named file value (probe-verified: scopeF->K missing).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: a scope frame is pushed on switch_case entry (empty at entry, so arm patterns still resolve outward); the payload binds into it and it pops at case exit. Fixture zig/bare-value-reads expects scopeF->K/scopeF->Limit and forbids Clue; mutant zig/switch-payload-scope CAUGHT. Lane replicas (pinned + 2 rotated seeds, zig + zls) 0/0.

decisions.question: Extreme review (2026-09-12): the function-entry walk bound EVERY identifier under a parameter node, so a name appearing only in a parameter's type, comptime type use, or default value shadowed the real file-level value for the whole function (the registered W9 defect: `s: struct { Flag: u8 }` swallowed `_ = Flag`; `x: T` swallowed the type use; `x: u32 = Def` swallowed the default read — all probe-verified missing pairs on both sides).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: a parameter binds its declared NAME only (first identifier child); payload binding unchanged (payload subtrees carry only capture names, probe-verified). Fixture zig/bare-value-reads expects typeField->Flag, takeT->T, withDefault->Def; mutant zig/param-subtree-bindings CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Extreme review (2026-09-12): `var _ = 1;` minted a `_` Variable symbol (GO5 class, probe-verified) — the read discipline already skipped blanks, but extraction did not.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: blank names skipped at all three declaration sites (variable, container field, function). Fixture zig/bare-value-reads forbids any `_` symbol; mutant zig/blank-symbol CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Extreme review (2026-09-12): an @import inside a function body was dropped entirely (locals-are-artifacts overreach) while calls in function bodies are captured — inconsistent evidence.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: the import fact and its reference edge are recorded exactly like the top-level branch, without minting a local symbol. Fixture zig/bare-value-reads expects the helper.zig import; mutant zig/drop-local-import CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Extreme review (2026-09-12): an if/while capture is bound into the enclosing frame, so a same-named file value read in the ELSE arm is suppressed (probe-verified: else-branch `v` reads nothing though the capture is not in scope there).
decisions.resolution: DOCUMENTED LIMITATION, not changed: scoping captures out of else-arms needs arm-level frames the single-pass walk cannot place (the capture is bound before the then/else split is known), and pushing a construct-level frame would trade one false negative for another. Both sides behave identically (lane-stable), and the shape needs a file value colliding with a capture name plus a same-named else-arm read to be observable.

decisions.question: The kind of a container-scope `const` was decided by a five-node value list and then by the NAME's case, which published a bit-shift as a `type` (838 corpus sites), a negation (39), a null-coercion (18), an anonymous tuple (22), an index (4), a catch (4) and a labeled block (9) as types, and published a type ALIAS as a value: `builtin_type` sat in the value list, so `const Pos = c_long;` was a `constant` (440 sites, 160 upper-case), as were `pointer_type` (55), `nullable_type` (31) and `array_type` (10).
decisions.resolution: FIXED: a node type that CAN be a type makes the declaration a Type; one that CANNOT makes it a value; only the two-sided forms (`identifier`, `field_expression`, `call_expression`, `if_expression`, `switch_expression`, `struct_initializer`, `parenthesized_expression`, `builtin_function`) keep the name heuristic, which is the pinned `pub const B = A` contract. One initializer IS a type — an array/slice of types (`[_]type{gtk.Scrollable}`) — and is tested on its element type. GATED: fixture zig/kinds-and-owners pins 13 kinds including the negative ones; mutants zig/type-alias-as-constant, zig/value-rhs-as-type, zig/labeled-block-as-type, zig/value-rhs-as-type (both directions) all CAUGHT. The remaining two-sided shapes are declared as ZIG.GAP.4 with their counts.

decisions.question: `opaque {}` is a container in Zig — no fields, but real declarations. The walk did not recognise it (`isContainer` named four node types), so every declaration inside came out as a free file-scope symbol: `pub fn create()` a `function` with no `scope`/`ownerName` and no `contains` edge. 123 opaque containers / 352 declarations in the pinned corpora; the kind guard was `container.kind !== Type`, a proxy for "a type alias has no body" that an opaque container (published as `Type`, because the shared SymbolKind has no Opaque member) did not satisfy.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: `opaque_declaration` joins the container set and ownership, not the kind, decides Method-vs-Function. 90% of the 352 declarations are now owned; the residue is nested containers whose members are owned by the inner type. GATED: fixture zig/kinds-and-owners (kind `method`, ownerName `Handle`, three `contains` rows); mutant zig/opaque-not-a-container CAUGHT.

decisions.question: The leaf was "the last identifier anywhere under the declaration, drop the first as the name", and the grammar never agreed to that story: it hands the type over as a FIELD (`parameter.type` 78,895, `container_field.type` 49,424, `variable_declaration.type` 43,949, `function_declaration.type` 37,129 in the pinned corpora). The walk was wrong wherever a declaration has a default value (`size: Size = .byte` published the enum member `byte`; `weight: Weight = c.FC_WEIGHT_THIN` published a C constant; `normal = @sizeOf(u8)` published a builtin), and where a type names nothing (an anonymous struct type in a parameter position published its FIELD name; an error set published a member, because `!T` keeps its dependency in the `ok` half and the walk took the last identifier of the whole union).
decisions.resolution: FIXED: the leaf is read from the `type` field, with the anonymous-container / error-set / `ok`-half / labeled-block cases returning nothing on purpose. No TYPE node carries a `type` field, so preferring it can never take the wrong side of a `!` (measured: `error_union_type` carries `ok` 21,353 and `error` 6,792, and no `type`). GATED: fixture zig/declared-type-leaf (7 expect rows, 8 forbid rows); mutants zig/default-value-as-type and zig/unnamed-type-publishes CAUGHT. Corpus effect measured by the oracle red-team: 702 phantom and 660 lost declared-type targets per 400 files under the pre-fix leaf.

decisions.node_type: the references class had no oracle
decisions.question: The differential compared only `calls` and `uses` for this lane, and the allowlist dropped the analyzer's own `references` edges from the compared side — so the largest emitted class on the zig corpora (declared-type dependencies plus imports) was compared against NOTHING, and the lane reported 100% coverage with phantom type references in the graph. This is the class the M14 completeness ledger warns about: an ABSENT capability emits nothing, and here a PRESENT capability emitted nothing checkable.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: `deriveZigReferenceEdges` derives the class from the tree (imports from `@import`/`@cImport` under a declaration RHS or a usingnamespace; declared types from the `type` field with the leaf rules), and `references` joins zig's compared labels. INDEPENDENCE: every position and leaf is re-derived; the only shared object is `ZIG_DECLARED_TYPE_BUILTINS`, the type-name vocabulary, imported from the analyzer per the #916 rule. RED-TEAM (M14 §5.7): the same comparison run against a pre-fix leaf transcription convicts it — 702 unexplained / 660 missing over 400 files — so the audit is not a tautology. Scope: the canonical M14.0.F5 artifact is emitted by the full ceremony sweep and is re-emitted there, as for the nim lane's join.

decisions.question: The ZGD1 write gate tested the NODE and not the OPERATOR, so it also swallowed the READ of every compound assignment. `self.n += 1;` reads `self.n`; `while (i < n) : (i += 1)` is Zig's own read-modify-write idiom. Measured: 280 compound field/index/dereference assignments in the pinned corpora, plus 1,837 compound bare-identifier forms (mostly locals, which the resolvability rule already excludes).
decisions.resolution: FIXED: a plain `=` is a write; every other operator is a read-modify-write, and the grammar separates them as distinct anonymous token types. Both surfaces moved together — the field-uses gate and the bare-identifier `isDefiningOccurrence` — because a global written with `+=` was invisible to the read graph in exactly the same way. GATED: zig/calls-uses-complexity now expects `uses bump -> n` and forbids only the plain write `uses set -> n`; mutant zig/compound-write-gate CAUGHT.

decisions.question: The family declares four declared-type positions (field, parameter, return, local) and the collector covered three. A `variable_declaration` carries a `type` field 43,949 times in the pinned corpora, and a local annotation was simply not read.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: the fourth position is collected, sharing the analyzer's per-file `emitted` dedupe with the other three so the overlap cannot become a second edge. GATED: fixture zig/declared-type-leaf uses a type named nowhere else in the file (`Only`) so the dedupe cannot hide the position; mutant zig/local-annotation-dropped CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Four helpers were defined and never called — `nameLine` (the C/C++ lanes' attribute-line-base helper, so the zig lane had no #920 line rule to claim), `zigTypeLeaf`, `zigCalleeLeaf`, `zigFieldLeaf` — and two payload paths asked for one of five node types where the grammar names the type as a FIELD: a property's `returnType` and a parameter's `type` were empty for every NAMED type, every array, every generic application and every qualified name.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: the four dead helpers removed (dead code in a review wave is a claim about a contract that is not implemented); both payloads read the field, which is how the nim lane (the most recent) publishes a property's type. GATED: fixture zig/declared-type-leaf pins `returnType` on named/array/optional properties and `expectParameters` on qualified, anonymous-struct and quoted-identifier parameters; mutants zig/field-type-list and zig/param-type-list CAUGHT.

decisions.node_type: the last regex in the analyzer
decisions.question: `/[!*/\s\[\]\{\}]+/g` sat on the declared-type path, where the receiver can only be an `identifier` node's text. On a plain identifier — `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, with no `<or>` and no `=` — all three surgeries on that line (the junk strip, the `<or>` split, the `=` split) are provable no-ops. On a QUOTED identifier they corrupt a legitimate name: the pinned corpora hold 34,132 quoted identifiers (`@"const"`, `@"or"`, `@"and"`, `@"enum"`, `@"zig lib"`, `@"weird function name"`), of which 1,916 carry a character from the junk class, and the pre-fix target for `@"zig lib"` was `@"ziglib"`.
decisions.resolution: REMOVED: the source spelling is published, which is what every other surface of this analyzer already publishes (symbol names, `uses` field leaves, call leaves), so edges resolve inside the index and the graph stays internally consistent. The two surviving tests are a `Set` membership and a character-code range. GATED: fixture zig/declared-type-leaf pins `@"weird type"` as the target and FORBIDS the corrupted `@"weirdtype"`; mutant zig/quoted-identifier-mangled CAUGHT. The lane is now zero-regex; the register row and the policy doc's declared count are re-emitted with the census.

decisions.node_type: labeled block is an executable body
decisions.question: ZGD3's rule — a `var`/`const` inside an executable body is an execution artifact — was written on the two node types that usually wrap a block (`test_declaration`, `comptime_declaration`). A LABELED BLOCK is the same kind of body reached by a different path, and its comptime locals were published as file-scope symbols: 70 symbols inside 35 block-shaped container-scope declarations over 400 corpus files, 27 of them `contains` edges attributing a block local to the enclosing container TWO levels above where it was written (`Action contains key_fields` for a local of a `cvalue: { … }` block inside an enum).
decisions.resolution: FIXED: the rule moved onto the `block` itself — in tree-sitter-zig `{ … }` is a body, never a type and never a declaration scope — which covers test blocks, comptime blocks, labeled blocks and `comptime_expression` alike. A/B on 800 files: 161 spurious symbols removed, 10 added, 23 GENUINE `uses` edges gained (a labeled-block value is readable, and before the fix it was published as a `type`, which does not resolve as a value), 27 fabricated `contains` edges removed. GATED: fixture zig/kinds-and-owners forbids `scratch`/`total`/`step` and their `contains` edges; mutant zig/block-locals-leak CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Every `pub const` at ANY level was pushed into the `exports` array. An export must name an IMPORTABLE unit; a member is reached as `Container.member`, which is the `contains` edge's job, so the entry invented a binding no importer can use. The class was latent until Z12 gave an opaque type its members — the fixture runner's export invariant caught it immediately ("export(s) [\"tag\"] do not resolve to a top-level symbol"), which is the honest way to find it.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: only a file-scope declaration enters `exports`; the `pub` fact survives as the member's `visibility`. GATED: the export invariant in the runner is the check (it fails the fixture when the row returns); mutant zig/container-member-exported CAUGHT.

decisions.question: A container declaration was only recognised as a container when it was a declaration's RIGHT-HAND SIDE. The same node reached as an EXPRESSION — an `if`/`switch` branch, a struct literal in a prune, a struct type inside a `nullable_type`/`array_type` — established no container, so its declarations were published as members of whatever enclosed them: a union variant's payload fields became members of the UNION, and two variants declaring the same field produced two symbols under ONE (owner, name) identity. Found as the residual of the Z19 A/B, not by a gate.
decisions.resolution: FIXED with an explicit ANONYMOUS CONTAINER branch and a third piece of walk context, so the rule is container IDENTITY rather than a proxy. Measured over 900 corpus files: 693 expression-position containers, 412 symbols inside, 379 mis-owned. A/B over 800 files: 422 symbols and 311 relationships (308 fabricated `contains`, 3 `uses`) removed with 0 added. Reads, calls and imports inside such a container are deliberately untouched. GATED by zig/kinds-and-owners (4 forbidSymbols, 4 forbidRelationships, 2 new expectRelationships) and mutation zig/anonymous-container-owns. Declared cost: a callable member of an unnamed type (`RtPreExecInfo.init`) is no longer indexed, because publishing it would require choosing between two readings of the same shape that the grammar cannot separate — see master-review.md.

decisions.question: A CONTAINER declared inside an executable body is a LOCAL type, and the walk handed its declarations to the ENCLOSING container: `const Local = struct { pub fn helper(v: T) void }` inside a method of `Host` published `helper` as a Method owned by `Host`, with a `contains Host -> helper` edge. Found by the ownership verifier, not by a gate - and not by the differential, which CANNOT see it: its coverage match is `label + normTarget(target)` and the source is not part of the key, so an edge that keeps its member name and changes owner still reads as covered.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: a container reached from an executable-body declaration is walked as an ANONYMOUS container, the same contract as the two sibling rulings (a container with no stable identity owns nothing), and the reads, calls and imports inside it are untouched. GATED by zig/kinds-and-owners (2 forbidSymbols, 2 forbidRelationships) and mutation zig/local-container-owns, and by the ownership verifier itself: 3,000 corpus files now report PHANTOM_OWN 0 and ORPHAN 0.

decisions.node_type: ownerSymbolId resolution (indexer), not an analyzer node type
decisions.status: RESOLVED — and the filing premise was wrong (Z49). The store resolves every same-named-container case by extent; 0 remain genuinely ambiguous.
decisions.question: Ownership is carried as a container NAME and the indexer resolves it by NAME within a file (`nameToSymbol.get(ownerName)` in parallel-indexer.ts), so two same-named containers in one file conflate every member under one `owner_symbol_id`. Measured by the ownership verifier over 3,000 corpus files: 1,509 member sites in 93 files, 100% from same-named containers, 0 genuine duplicates; the worst file declares `pub const C = extern struct { key, value }` FIFTEEN times. The analyzer is faithful at its boundary - 15 distinct `C` symbols and 30 distinct `key` symbols, each with its own range and line - so the defect is the ownership TOKEN, not the extraction.
decisions.resolution: NOT FIXED by the lane, and the reason is the boundary: both candidate fixes cross layers. (1) Indexer-side, smallest: when a name maps to more than one container in a file, resolve the owner by the nearest ENCLOSING declaration range - the mechanism already exists for the no-owner path (range-containment Tier 1, nearest-preceding-container Tier 2). (2) Analyzer-side: carry a unique owner identity (`Target.C`), which changes `scope`/`ownerName`, every `contains` edge source and every hover label - a family-visible contract change. Filed as #963 with the measurement; the lane gates the class it can fix and hands the owner the two options rather than choosing a contract unilaterally. Related: #924 (the quoted-name surface, same 'family contract, not a lane fix' shape).

decisions.node_type: n/a — a defect in the F5 GATE, not in the analyzer
decisions.status: FIXED + GATED (the gate was wrong; the analyzer was right)
decisions.question: F5 read 970 MISSING on one 200-file draw and 0 on another, with the same analyzer, the same corpus and the same comparison code — and the number moved with the DRAW. The bare-read truth's `isDefining` carried Z15's plain-`=` operator test as an early `return false` for EVERY parent, so it short-circuited its own declaration branch: the truth derived a `uses` row for the name of every function and field it walked, including the `pub fn init(` line itself. Every one of the phantom rows was provenance-checked to the declaration site, not to a use. Size: one phantom row per file-scope declaration, which is exactly why a rotating draw reported it as 0 on one run and 970 on the next.
decisions.resolution: FIXED in the truth, not in the analyzer: the operator test belongs to the assignment-shaped parents (`variable_declaration`, `assignment_expression`, `compound_assignment_statement`, `assignment_statement`) and now runs inside that branch, so the declaration branch is reachable again. The analyzer was never wrong — it had never emitted those edges. GATED by a new assertion in the oracle red-team (case [3]): a truth `uses` row whose target is a file-scope declaration name must have a genuine bare read site for that name, computed from the tree. 0 violations on 200 files; the pre-Z24 shape SIMULATED on the same files raises 2,512, so the assertion can fail. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE: a gate that reports a class it has not adjudicated is worse than no gate, because the class is read as an analyzer defect and the fix goes into the wrong file. Z19/Z21/Z22 were all found by an independent instrument; this one was found by the instrument disagreeing with itself across draws, which is the only reason it was caught at all.

decisions.node_type: n/a — a second defect in the F5 truth, same family as Z24
decisions.status: FIXED + GATED (the analyzer was right in all 7 rows)
decisions.question: After Z24, F5's residual was 7-8 UNEXPLAINED rows per 100-200-file draw, and all of them had one shape: a bare read of a FILE-SCOPE name in the VALUE position of a struct-literal field assignment - `.{ .id = base_id }`, `.{ .deinit = deinit, .parserHandler = parserHandler }`, `&.{ .concurrent = concurrent, .select = select }`. The truth's `isDefining` matched 'the first named child of type `identifier`', but in a struct literal the KEY is a `field_identifier`, so the first identifier child IS THE VALUE - and the truth read each of those as a definition and dropped the read. The analyzer published all of them, correctly.
decisions.resolution: FIXED in the truth: the LHS test is now NODE IDENTITY with the first named child, which is the same rule the ZGD1 field-path mirror in the same file already used - one rule, two places. MEASURED: the oracle red-team's case 3 (a truth `uses` row whose target is a file-scope declaration name must have a genuine bare read site) went from 34 to 48 genuine reads on 200 files with violations still 0, i.e. the newly-derived rows are reads, not declarations. WHY IT MATTERS: this class was INVISIBLE in both directions - it could not read as a miss (the truth never derived it) nor as a defect (the analyzer's row looked like noise), and the natural reaction to unexplained rows is to delete them from the analyzer. Two gate defects in a row, both pointing at the analyzer, is what made the pattern worth chasing rather than dismissing.

decisions.question: `contains` was 16.6% of everything this analyzer emits (5,521 of 33,266 relationships over 400 corpus files) and NOTHING had ever adjudicated it, for a structural reason: the analyzer derives containment from `symbol.ownerName`, a field its own walk sets, so the class is self-agreeing. The new gate found two fabrications of methods that DO NOT EXIST. A function-pointer type parses as container_field > pointer_type > function_signature, and a function_signature has no `declarator` field at all, so the old anyChild(identifier) name-picking took whatever identifier came first under the node: the RETURN TYPE (`contains MutableArray -> ComparisonResult`) or a qualified segment of a parameter type (`contains Options -> apprt`, out of `*apprt.ClipboardRequest`).
decisions.resolution: FIXED: a `function_signature` is a TYPE, so it no longer goes on the declaration path; its children are still walked, because a function type's parameters and return type are declared-type facts the `references` collection reads on purpose. GATED by zig/kinds-and-owners (3 forbidSymbols, 2 forbidRelationships), mutation zig/function-signature-is-a-method, and the contains gate itself, which reads 0 PHANTOM / 0 MISSING over 400 files where it read 2 PHANTOM before the fix. THE METHODOLOGICAL PART, and the reason this is filed as a decision and not a chore: the ownership verifier could NOT find it, because its derivation used the same first-identifier rule and therefore AGREED with the bug. A mirror that reproduces the defect it exists to convict is self-agreeing, so the new truth was written from the GRAMMAR — which is also the only test of a mirror: a rule that needs the analyzer's own output to state is not a mirror.

decisions.question: With a truth for `contains` written, the obvious move was to add the label to F5's compared set and call the class covered. Measured, that is half: the F5 matcher keys on `label + normTarget(target)` and the SOURCE is not part of the key, so `contains` is compared BY MEMBER NAME. It convicts a fabricated or missing edge whose NAME is wrong and is blind to one whose OWNER is wrong — and Z19 and Z21 each moved 335 edges to a different owner while keeping every member name.
decisions.resolution: BOTH, with the split stated rather than implied. (1) `deriveZigContainment` walks the TREE and rebuilds the owner chain, and `contains` joins F5's compared set for zig: that catches fabrication and loss at name level, in the shared gate, on every lane-run. (2) `script/m14/tmp/zigw-contains.ts` keys on the OWNER and is BIDIRECTIONAL — it asks both directions: is every PUBLISHED owner justifiable (the ownership verifier's question, and how Z22 was found), and is a justifiable owner MISSING (a question the verifier could not ask, because it only ever iterated published symbols, so extra derived pairs were invisible). The second direction is what makes a dropped ownership detectable at all. (3) The store-identity collisions stay REPORTED and not failed: 1,509 member sites in 93 files, 100% same-named containers, filed as #963 — the defect is the store's name-keyed owner lookup and no analyzer change can fix it. Two instruments, one class, and the part neither covers is written down instead of inferred from a clean count.

decisions.question: The container-field extraction required `length < 50` and the function extraction `length < 100`, so a length test was acting as a junk filter on NAMES. Measured over 1,200 corpus files: 14 of 27,004 named container fields (0.05%) are 50 characters or longer and were dropped outright — an LSP capability flag 74 characters long (`supports_workspace_did_change_configuration_dynamic_registration`) and the aro `__builtin_amdgcn_wmma_*` shims at 50-52. The F5 `contains` truth found it as 1 MISSING row on zls, and it is a LOSS class: no count of published symbols can show a declaration that is absent.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: the field name is read from the grammar's own `name` FIELD and the function name POSITIONALLY (this grammar has no `declarator` field on a function_declaration — measured: `function_declaration [fields: type]`, first named child is always the name). The field is read only when it is an identifier: an unnamed `extern struct` member hands over a TYPE there, and the first version of the change published four fields named after their own type (`usize`, `isize`, `c_short`, `c_int` in zls/src/analyser/InternPool.zig) — 31 fabricated `contains` edges in one file, which the `contains` gate caught in the OPPOSITE direction from the one that found the loss. Caps remain (200 / 100) and are now stated as the guards they are: measured, 0 field names reach 100 characters. GATED by zig/kinds-and-owners (2 expectSymbols) and mutation zig/long-field-name-dropped. The deep `anyChild(identifier)` search is gone from both common paths, which is also what Z26 needed.

decisions.question: The predicate that decides 'write or read' was spelled three different ways, and all three were wrong somewhere. In the differential's truth it was wrong twice (Z24, Z25). In the analyzer it tested 'the first named child of type `identifier`', which is not the LHS when the left side is a field expression: in `exe.stack_size = stack_size` (zig/build.zig:727) the first identifier child is the VALUE, so the read of a file-scope constant was declared a definition and no `uses` was published. One row in 1,200 files, and the analyzer's own `isWriteLhs` — 600 lines away, on the field-read path — already had the correct form.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: `isDefiningOccurrence` now uses node identity against the first named child, which is what `isWriteLhs` already did, so the two sites in the file are one rule instead of two spellings. Z15's compound-assignment behaviour is preserved by the `isPlainAssignment` guard above it. GATED by zig/kinds-and-owners (2 expectSymbols, 2 expectRelationships on the read side) and mutation zig/field-assignment-rhs-read. The general finding is the one worth keeping: a LOSS and a FABRICATION from ONE line, and each needed a different instrument — a `should be published` oracle for the first, a `contains` oracle for the second. Neither is visible to a count of what the analyzer emitted.

decisions.question: The lane recorded every import correctly and published NONE of them as an `imports` relationship, which 16 analyzers emit and which the graph engine, the brain's evidence enrichment and the MCP handler all read — so `bb_graph` filtered on `imports` returned nothing for zig. Measured over 400 corpus files: 1,458 facts, 394 distinct module targets, and 176 targets containing a path separator (`../global.zig`, `../build/gresource.zig`) — strings no zig declaration name can hold, which is go's own argument for moving import edges off `references`.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: every import site gets BOTH labels, the path literal's line on each (M60.A7). The `references` twin STAYS — it is the edge this lane's declared-type/reference truth derives — so the change ADDS a class rather than reclassifying one. Implemented as a SITE PASS, not a fourth shape test, after the third shape test lost 460 of 1,918 sites (24%): an import used as a PREFIX on a longer expression (`@import("build.zig.zon").version`, `try @import("apple_sdk").addPaths(b, lib)`) reached none of the three shape branches. GATED by script/m14/tmp/zigw-imports.ts, keyed on `(target, line)` because import facts are per-SITE, and bidirectional. The gate convicted my own partial fix on its first run — which is the argument for it.

decisions.question: #924's E half (a7368a80) canonicalizes quoting out of a published NAME and out of every relationship source and target, but not out of the symbol's TYPE-BEARING payload — so one declared type was published two ways in one result: `references (declared-type) -> weird type` beside `returnType: @"weird type"`.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: the canonicalization pass now covers returnType, every parameter's type and name, genericParameters, decorators and comments. A consumer that resolves a symbol by matching its declared type against a published name or an edge target could not resolve a quoted type at all — the same class Z18 fixed on the edge side. The class is 0 of 8,273 symbols over 400 corpus files, which is exactly why a SYNTHETIC fixture is the instrument: a census reads 0 and the defect is still live. GATED by zig/declared-type-leaf and zig/relationship-classes.

decisions.question: ZIG.D.1 ruled `instantiates` out on the grounds that generics are "compile-time monomorphized without a runtime type dispatch the analyzer can attribute statically". The premise is measurably false for two classes: a `fn … type` is a DECLARATION in the file, so every call to it is a statically derivable type application, and `TypeName{ … }` is a construction of an in-file type — which is exactly the class ZIG.GAP.3 has wanted since it was written, and for which the family's mechanism IS this relationship type (c/cpp with `isConstructor`, clojure, clean).
decisions.resolution: FIXED: 132 edges over 400 corpus files — 77 constructions, 55 generic applications — written the way those lanes write it: source is the enclosing symbol or `(global)`, the target must be a type DECLARED IN THIS FILE (so the edge is proven: confidence 1.0, `isExternalTarget: false`), and the line is the HEAD node's. Nothing was reclassified; the existing `uses`/`references` edges stay. GATED by script/m14/tmp/zigw-instantiation.ts, which counts the two classes separately so a regression in one is attributable, and which caught its own mirror being incomplete: the first rule accepted only a bare identifier head and read 2 PHANTOM rows on the QUALIFIED constructions (`Color.C{ .r = 1 }`, `T.KV{ .key = 0 }`) that zig code is full of. KNOWN LIMIT, stated: only in-file targets. A qualified or external generic application (`std.ArrayList(u8)`) is a real instantiation that neither side publishes, and measuring it needs a cross-file type index — a different instrument, not a fix here. ZIG.D.1's ruling for extends/implements/overrides is unaffected and still correct: zig has no inheritance at all.

decisions.question: The relationship census (script/m14/zig-relationship-census.ts) reads the engine's type list from the SOURCE and requires every type to be emitted-and-gated or ruled with a reason. It caught its own lane: `exports` was unclassified, and checking it turned out to be a real gap — 1,465 exported declarations in 391 of 400 corpus files (673 functions, 252 type aliases, 222 structs, 168 enums, 123 constants, 26 unions, 1 variable), recorded in `res.exports` and published as no relationship at all.
decisions.resolution: FIXED: one `exports` relationship per exported declaration, GENERATED FROM the export list so the array and the edges cannot drift — the failure the `imports` twins had already paid for once. Source is `(file)`, deliberately not `(global)`, which is this lane's marker for the expression scope reads and imports are attributed to; keeping them apart lets a consumer group an API surface without guessing a convention. A `pub` INSIDE a container is still not an export (Z20: 1,720 of them in the same sample are `contains` edges and visibilities). GATED by script/m14/tmp/zigw-exports.ts, bidirectional so the array drifting from the edges is also caught. The export list gained a `range` so the edge can carry the name's own line (M59.A7/M60); the interface always had the optional field and nothing populated it.

decisions.question: An `@import` BINDING minted a symbol only when its right-hand side was LONGER than the import itself: `const std = @import("std")` published no symbol, `const longer = @import("std").ArrayList` published one, and the same file could have both. That is not a rule any language has. Three costs, all measured: the module's own namespace was missing its most common declaration (1,458 bindings in 400 corpus files), a `pub const X = @import(...)` re-export — the canonical zig re-export idiom — named a binding the index could not resolve (the fixture runner's export invariant caught it, a general check this lane did not have to write), and the binding was invisible while the import EDGE was perfect.
decisions.resolution: FIXED by REMOVING an early exit rather than adding a rule: at file or container scope the walk now falls through to the same const/var handling every other declaration gets, so kind, visibility and owner are decided in one place. Inside a function body the exit stays — Z9, and the family's LocalsAreNotSymbols rule. The binding is marked `zigImportBinding` so the fact is queryable and the regression is reconstructible by a marker rather than a name list. The lane's own contains-mirror had encoded the old behaviour as a rule, and the gate read 4 PHANTOM rows on exactly the container-scope aliases it used to exclude: a mirror written against yesterday's contract is not a mirror, it is a second opinion of the wrong thing.

decisions.question: After #924-E, the tree's spelling and the PUBLISHED spelling differ: `@"1Monochrome"` in the tree, `1Monochrome` published. The contains mirror derived the tree's text and the comparison is against the published surface, so it read 75 PHANTOM and 75 MISSING on one shape — an enum whose members begin with a digit, which zig therefore makes you quote.
decisions.resolution: RULED, and the fix is structural rather than another patch: `stripZigQuoting` is now EXPORTED from the analyzer and the truths IMPORT it, because a copied canonicalization rule is a rule that will drift. A mirror must derive from the tree but must publish the analyzer's spelling, and the cheapest way to guarantee that is not to re-implement the rule.

decisions.question: Every analyzer in this family classifies each edge it publishes, and the classification is CONSUMED: the MCP handler's tierFor returns a STORED metadata.evidenceClass in preference to one derived from the relationship type, so a wrong stored value beats a correct derivation. Wave 4 added `imports` and `exports` and no gate on this lane asked whether the new classes survived the pipeline. They did not: both fell through to the default and were published as `usage_contextual`, so a module DEPENDENCY and a published API name were both reported as usage. And the `instantiates` branch read `md.confidence` and `md.isConstructor` — two fields this lane never sets — so it returned `structural` by ACCIDENT rather than by decision.
decisions.resolution: FIXED to the family rule that ~26 analyzers state explicitly (objc/c/clean/yaml): contains → structural, imports/exports/references → import_based, calls/uses → usage_contextual, instantiates → structural when proven in-file (the pass writes isExternalTarget:false) and inferred otherwise. GATED by script/m14/tmp/zigw-evidence-tier.ts, whose expected table was written from the FAMILY'S rule rather than from this lane's output — and which reported 5 of 7 types wrong on its first run, which is the calibration that makes a clean run mean something. NOT pinned by the fixture: the runner's matchConstraints does not apply relationship-metadata keys and says so ('inert assertion') rather than accepting a row that asserts nothing, so the tier is a probe. THE QUESTION THAT FOUND IT is the transferable one: does a NEW class survive the graph, the store and the MCP handler? No gate on this lane was asking, and a class that is emitted, gated and scored can still be mislabelled everywhere downstream.

decisions.node_type: the SOURCE of every `uses` and `calls` edge
decisions.status: FIXED — gate clean in BOTH directions (0 phantom, 0 missing)
decisions.question: `uses` and `calls` are 24,743 of the lane's 38,271 relationships, and the only instrument that judged them keys on `label + normTarget(target)` — which DISCARDS the source. A read attributed to the wrong function is a wrong graph, and a name-level gate cannot see it: that is the Z22 shape one class up, and Z19/Z21/Z22 between them moved hundreds of edges between owners while every member name stayed the same. Worse, the truths that would judge it lived in the shared differential, and the 2026-09-29 merge came back with a THIRD variant of the bare-read one — no Z15 operator test, no Z24 branch scoping, Z25's node-identity test reverted — which is why the seven-class F5 draw read 17 MISSING / 43 unexplained while a direct per-file comparison against the lane's own truth agreed exactly.
decisions.resolution: The two edge truths moved to script/m14/zig-truth.ts (lane-owned, has survived three merges of the shared file untouched) and now CARRY THE SOURCE, so `zigw-uses-calls.ts` can compare the axis the shared matcher discards. The gate compares SOURCE SETS per (label, target), not (source,target,line) as a key: keying on the source re-litigates whether the row EXISTS — a question the name-level agreement already settled — and buries the one that has no answer yet. First run: 645 disagreements, of which 642 were the INSTRUMENT: both truths deduped by NAME while the analyzer dedupes by (source, name), so the first site claimed a name and every later read from another function was suppressed — and the rows that survived were attributed to the WRONG function, the same defect the gate exists to find. With the keys fixed and Z34's canonicalization applied to the read targets: **PHANTOM 0, MISSING 0, 4,590 source agreements over 200 files** — the class closed in BOTH directions. The last 49 were a rule CONFLATED BETWEEN TWO PASSES: Z38's type-position walk was written into the bare-read pass's `underField` test, but that test is the LEAF-ONLY contract (a field path owns its member leaf and the objects along it) and is unconditional — the walk belongs to the FIELD pass, where a dotted TYPE path's segments are declared-type facts. With the walk in both places the mirror published 58 file-scope `uses -> std` rows the analyzer correctly does not. THE LESSON, which is the transferable one: one rule per site, and the site that owns it — a fix in one pass is not the same rule as the fix in another, and assuming otherwise is how a mirror invents 49 defects out of one correct change.

decisions.status: FIXED + GATED (fixture + mutant + the source-keyed gate)
decisions.question: The type-position guard in the field/call pass tested only the DIRECT parent (`parameter`, `container_field`, `function_declaration`). In this grammar `std.Build.LazyPath` is a CHAIN of `field_expression` nodes, so every SEGMENT of a qualified type in a signature had a `field_expression` parent, none was recognised as a type position, and each was published as a `uses` READ of a type name — attributed to the function whose signature it appears in, and duplicating the declared-type class that already publishes `references (declared-type) -> Build` for the same text.
decisions.resolution: The test now walks the chain: a field_expression is in a type position when any ancestor — through the dotted path only, stopping at the value contexts the analyzer already knows (call, block, assignment, declaration-with-value, struct literal, return/if/switch/while/for) — is a parameter, a container field, or a declared return type. Bounded deliberately, because a type path that reaches a value context is a VALUE read whatever its base looks like. Measured by the source-keyed gate: 480 of the first run's 645 disagreements were this one shape, and they are invisible at name level because the target is a real type name. GATED by zig/relationship-classes (3 forbidRelationships on the type-path segments) and mutation zig/dotted-type-path-read — whose FIRST VERSION HAD THE DIRECTION BACKWARDS: it removed the fabricated edges, which is the state the FIX produces, so it passed and the suite correctly reported a survivor. The pre-fix state ADDS them.

decisions.node_type: the SOURCE of an edge inside a named `test`
decisions.status: FIXED (both passes) — gated by the source-keyed gate
decisions.question: A named `test` is a scope with a name, and NEITHER source-attribution pass recognised it: the field/call pass set `nextFn` for `function_declaration` only, and the bare-read pass built its `fnName` frame for `function_declaration` only. So every call and read inside `test ParagraphStyle { const p = try ParagraphStyle.create(&.{}); defer p.release(); }` was attributed to `(global)` — a file-scope source for work plainly inside one named block. Three rows in 200 files, and the class is not three rows: it is every read and call in every named test in the corpus, invisible to the shared matcher because that discards the source.
decisions.resolution: Both passes now treat `test_declaration` as a named scope, so the two sites in the file agree on what a named scope is — which is the point, because two spellings of one rule is how Z24, Z25 and Z29 happened. The source-keyed gate convicts it: the wrong-source class went to zero. GATED by zig/relationship-classes (one expectRelationship on the test's own source, plus the file-scope value it reads) and mutation zig/test-scope-reads-attributed-to-global.

decisions.wave: 6 — the name-level axis, and the last unexplained class on the corpus
decisions.status: TRUTH BEHIND — fixed and gated (the analyzer was right)
decisions.observation: F5 reported 9 of 6,375 analyzer edges `unexplained` on its Zig draw, with no sample: a count nobody can act on. The lane's five gates were all 0/0, because they compare per SITE (imports/exports), per OWNER KEY (contains) or per (label, target, source-set) (uses/calls) — and an edge that NO truth row accounts for is invisible to every one of them. So the finding needed its own instrument.
decisions.analysis: The class was the `references` TWIN of `@import`. Since Z30 the analyzer has published, for every import site, `imports <path literal>` for the module and `references <path literal>` for the same literal on the same line, tiered `import_based` rather than `declared_type` — and NO truth derived the twin. 29 `references -> std` rows in 120 files, plus the same shape for path literals such as `src/dev.zig`. The twin is load-bearing, not decorative: `references` is the label the engine resolves names through, so an import whose module is absent there is a module the graph cannot reach. Its absence was a hole in the ORACLE, not a redundant edge to tidy away.
decisions.resolution: `deriveZigImportSites` is now ONE shared walk and both classes are built on it, because the alternative was the third spelling of the import rule and Z24/Z25/Z29 are all what that costs. `deriveZigReferenceEdges` gained the twin, emitted after the declared-type edges and deduped on its own `import-twin|target|line` key so a declared-type edge naming the same module stays visible as a separate row. New gate `script/m14/tmp/zigw-unexplained.ts` reports BOTH directions at name level. Result: UNEXPLAINED 0, MISSING 0 over 200 files and over 1,200.
decisions.cost: The gate exists because the shared harness could not be trusted to be runnable: HEAD's `differential.ts` had lost its `main()` to a merge and exited silently with status 0, and the worktree copy belongs to a lane mid-rewrite whose config names corpus repos this machine does not have. A gate that only runs when the shared harness runs is not a gate.

decisions.wave: 6 — found by the Z40 gate, on the row it did not raise
decisions.status: TRUTH BEHIND — fixed and gated (the analyzer was right)
decisions.observation: With Z40 closed, one class remained on a 1,200-file draw: `uses -> progress_normal {d}`, from `zig/lib/std/Progress.zig:1248`.
decisions.analysis: Not a format string after all. That file genuinely declares `const @"progress_normal {d}" = "\x1b]9;4;1;{d}\x1b\\";` — a legal Zig quoted identifier whose name happens to read like a format spec — and line 1248 reads it. Both the analyzer's symbol and its edge are correct. The MIRROR was comparing a stripped name against a raw one: the inventory is built from symbol names, and a quoted declaration's symbol name has its `@"..."` syntax stripped (Z34), while the node's own text still carries it, so the lookup could never match. Z34 was applied to the OUTPUT side and not to the LOOKUP side, and a rule applied on only one side of a comparison is not a rule.
decisions.resolution: The read name and the shadow set are canonicalized through the same `stripZigQuoting` the analyzer publishes with, so both sides of every comparison speak one spelling.

decisions.status: MEASURED AND DISCLOSED - no analyzer defect in any of the 93 files
decisions.observation: The lane had carried '219 of 3,839 files fail to parse' as an open item for its whole life, and the number was WRONG. Measured: 93 of 3,839 (2.4%) carry ERROR nodes - zig 86/2,950, zls 2/90, ghostty 5/799 - with 811 ERROR nodes, 0 MISSING nodes, across 69 shapes. The figure had been repeated without anyone re-running the instrument, which is what an unexamined number does: it survives because it is plausible, not because it is true.
decisions.method: tree-sitter is error-tolerant, so a dirty file still yields a tree and the analyzer still publishes for the regions it can read. That is why the population was never a blocker - and also why it was never EXPLANED. `script/m14/tmp/zigw-parse-errors.ts` buckets every dirty file; `zigw-parse-residual.ts` names the residue per file.
decisions.resolution: All 93 fall into four named buckets, and only three are grammar limitations: (1) 43 files are INTENTIONALLY invalid - 42 in zig/test/cases/compile_errors plus the langref page that exists to demonstrate an uninitialized `var` - where an ERROR node is the CORRECT answer and nothing is lost; (2) 45 use inline assembly, which the grammar cannot read (376 of the 811 ERROR nodes); (3) 2 declare a container field named after a Zig keyword (`async`/`await` in zig/lib/std/Io.zig and zls semantic_tokens.zig), which the grammar reads as an async/await expression; (4) 3 use a LABELED BLOCK in expression position - `std.c.environ[0..env_len: { ...break :env_len len; } :null]` in ghostty global.zig and main_c.zig, and a switch prong payload `.true => true: { ...break :true ...; }` in Surface.zig - which the grammar parses as an index_expression and breaks on at the `:null`.
decisions.cost: None of the three limitations is an ANALYZER defect, and none costs a relationship class: the five site gates, the source gate and the name-level gate are all 0/0 over 1,200 files drawn from these same three corpora. They are disclosed rather than fixed because the fix is a GRAMMAR change (tree-sitter-zig), which is not this lane's to make and not a change to the analyzer. The claim the lane can make is precise: on 97.6% of the corpus every published relationship is tree-derived, and on the remaining 2.4% the losses are confined to three named syntaxes rather than distributed invisibly.

decisions.wave: 8 - a gate that had been reporting a defect that did not exist
decisions.status: INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG - the analyzer was right; the ownership verifier is fixed and calibrated
decisions.observation: Asked to bring the docs up to date, the ownership row claimed `PHANTOM_OWN 0`. Re-running the instrument behind that number gave **701** - and `zigw-contains.ts`, which derives containment from the grammar and keys on the owner, reported 0/0 on the same edges. Two committed gates disagreed about the same relationships, so one of them was wrong and neither number could go in a document.
decisions.analysis: The verifier built its key as `owner~~member` and filled the DERIVED side from `firstIdent`, which returns an `identifier` node's `text`. In this grammar a quoted identifier is an `identifier` node whose text CARRIES its `@"..."` syntax, while the published SYMBOL name has that syntax stripped (Z34). So `@"1Monochrome"` was derived raw and compared against a published `1Monochrome`, and the key never matched. Two classes, both real Zig: quoted enum members whose C names begin with a digit (ghostty's macOS pixel-format bindings) and containers declared as `pub const @"can-remember" = struct { … }` in ghostty's GTK bindings. 701 phantoms, all of them correct analyzer edges.
decisions.resolution: Every name path in the verifier now goes through the analyzer's own `stripZigQuoting` - the member name, the error-set member, and the declaring container's name. Result at 3,000 files / 136,719 symbols: **AGREE 84,442, PHANTOM_OWN 0, ORPHAN 0, COLLISION 1,485** (1,480 same-named containers, 0 genuine duplicates), which is the #963 store defect and nothing else.
decisions.cost: This is the SIXTH instance of one mistake - a rule applied on one side of a comparison and not the other, after Z24, Z25, Z29, Z34 and Z41 - and the second time a DOCUMENT inherited a number from a document instead of from a run. The general finding is larger than the 701 rows: a gate that has never been calibrated against a known-good case is not evidence, and quoting an inherited figure is how `219 of 3,839` and `46/46` survived as long as they did. The verifier now also has a documented verdict, and the line-accuracy gate gained a `--shift` control so its 100% can be shown to fail on demand (it drops to 13.50%).

decisions.wave: 9 - the final review: the output channels nobody was auditing
decisions.status: FIXED - three classes had no reason code, and the complexity operators were pinned by nothing
decisions.observation: The lane has eleven gates and every one of them watches RELATIONSHIPS. Three whole output channels were ungated: SYMBOLS, COMPLEXITY and file-level metadata. A single invariant audit over a 300-file draw (1,110 symbols, 2,908 relationships, 319 functions) found 5 classes, of which 2 were the audit's own bugs and 3 were real.
decisions.analysis: REAL: `contains` (261 rows), `exports` (126) and `instantiates` (44) published NO `metadata.relationshipType` reason code, while the other four classes did. The doc promised that every heuristic edge carries a machine-readable reason; `contains` is the LARGEST class in the corpus and was the one that said nothing, because it is built from the symbol table at the end of the walk rather than at the member's site. NOT REAL, and now encoded as deliberate: 18 `calls` self-loops (recursion - `fn fibonacci` calling itself IS a call) and 27 same-(type,source,target) rows in the SITE-KEYED classes (`imports`, the import `references` twin, `instantiates`), where one edge per site is the contract while the other classes collapse per (source, target).
decisions.resolution: Reason codes added: `zig_ownership`, `zig_export`, `zig_instantiation`. Asserted on 7 fixture rows and pinned by mutant `zig/reason-code-dropped`, CALIBRATED by hand-removing the code and watching F3 go 7/7 -> 5/7. Separately, the complexity OPERATORS were counted by the implementation and pinned by NOTHING: `for`, `while`, `switch`, `and`, `or`, `orelse` and accumulation across two constructs. All eight values were hand-computed from the documented rule and matched on the first run - the implementation was right and the fixture was thin. Pinned now.
decisions.cost: The audit's own bugs were worth as much as its findings. It kept its duplicate-detection maps OUTSIDE the per-file loop, so it reported 1,392 'duplicates' that were the same edge in different files; and it looked for `metadata.complexity` when complexity lives at `symbol.complexity` (the family standard, as go/c/rust emit it), so it reported 319 functions with no complexity out of 319 that all had it. An instrument that manufactures violations is as expensive as one that hides them, and both were caught only by reading the samples rather than the counts.

decisions.wave: 9 - two dead branches, found by the gate that was already red
decisions.status: FIXED - no behaviour change; the F1 audit is green again
decisions.observation: `audit-analyzer-grammar.ts` reported `zig FAIL refs=52 unknown=2` while the analyzer doc AND the closure both claimed `PASS - 45 refs, 0 unknown`. The audit was right and both documents were stale.
decisions.analysis: The two unregistered type literals were `field_identifier` (a field's name node) and `struct_literal` (a construction). NEITHER EXISTS in the pinned grammar - probe-verified against the shipped wasm by `zigw-dead-branches.ts`: a field's name is an `identifier`, and a construction is a `struct_initializer` (`anonymous_struct_initializer` for `.{ ... }`). Both were dead disjuncts left by a grammar rename, and in both the LIVE disjunct was the first one, so no output was wrong: constructions were detected (132 per 400 files) and field names were read. The cost was not correctness but honesty - a second 'supported spelling' that could never match, in the class that instantiates.
decisions.resolution: Both dead disjuncts removed. F1: `zig PASS refs=50 unknown=0`. Note the ref count rose 45 -> 50 across Z37-Z39 and this wave, which is the count moving with the analyzer rather than a claim that had drifted.
decisions.cost: This is the second time in two days that a green figure in a Zig document was wrong and the instrument behind it was right. `PHANTOM_OWN 0` (Z43) and `F1 0 unknown` (Z45) were both inherited from an earlier document instead of from a run. The pattern is now specific enough to name: a lane that quotes its own history inherits its own errors.

decisions.wave: 10 - the lane's own F5, and the defect it found on its first run
decisions.status: FIXED - gated by a fixture on both sides, a mutant, and a new dangling-target invariant
decisions.observation: The lane had no F5 of its own: every published Zig number came from `differential.ts`, a shared file that has already lost its `main()` to a merge here and is mid-rewrite in the working tree. Building one (`zigw-lane-differential.ts`) was meant to make the table reproducible from this lane. Its FIRST run reported 1 MISSING in 400 files, and that was a real defect.
decisions.analysis: `ghostty/src/os/i18n.zig:69` declares `pub fn _(msgid: [*:0]const u8) [*:0]const u8` — the gettext convention, and the entire i18n entry point of ghostty. The analyzer refused to mint a symbol for it AND published `calls (global) -> _` at line 208: a DANGLING EDGE, a call into a name the index will never resolve. Cause: the blank-identifier rule (Z8/GO5), which is right for `const _ = 1;`, was ALSO applied to the function branch.
decisions.resolution: The refusal stays in the binding branch and leaves the function branch. Pinned on BOTH sides, because the contract is the distinction and a fixture asserting only the positive case would let the blanket refusal back: `pub fn _()` publishes a Function; `const _ = 42;` publishes nothing (forbidSymbols); the `calls -> _` edge has a declared target. Mutant `zig/underscore-fn-not-declared` SURVIVED the first attempt — it stripped the symbol but no fixture asserted on `_`, which is the correct verdict from a suite that had no such row. New invariant: an edge whose target is declared at FILE SCOPE with no published symbol is dangling. Verified by reverting the fix by hand and watching it fire.
decisions.cost: `zigw-lane-differential.ts` reproduces F5's semantics exactly (same `normTarget`, same `label + normTarget(target)` key) so its numbers are COMPARABLE, and adds the STRICT rule that keeps the dotted qualifier — the axis F5 offers only behind `BB_F5_STRICT` and the axis Z40 hid on. First run: 60,107 truth rows, 100.00% covered, 0 missing, 0 unexplained, and 0 on the strict axis too. Its own first version had an accounting bug (counting truth rows but covered KEYS, capping the ratio at 67% on a run where nothing was missing), which is the seventh time this lane has shipped a number that could not reach its own true value.

decisions.wave: 10 - a coverage question, asked four times, with three wrong answers
decisions.status: MEASURED - file-scope declaration coverage is 100.00%, and the instrument is now a gate
decisions.observation: A dangling `calls` edge implied declarations were being lost, so I measured file-scope declaration coverage over all 3,839 corpus files. Four versions of that question, three of them wrong:
decisions.resolution: v1 counted REGEX matches for column-0 `fn` against ownerless function symbols: 103% coverage, because the two populations are different sets. v2 compared the source's column-0 `fn` NAMES against published symbols: 18 files losing 164 declarations — which looked decisive and was not, because `aro/Builtins/*.zig` carries `// zig fmt: off`, so the members of a `return struct { … }` sit at column 0 and look file-scope while being members of an anonymous struct that Z22 correctly rules owns nothing. v3 derived file scope from the grammar by walking ancestors: 99.88%, 22 files short — still wrong, because a struct member's chain is `function_declaration < struct_declaration < source_file`, which crosses no statement barrier, so eight-space-indented members were counted as file-scope. v4 adds containers to the barrier set: **20,944 file-scope declarations, 20,944 published, 100.00%, zero files short, all three corpora.**
decisions.cost: Now a gate that exits non-zero below 100%. The general finding is larger than the number: this lane produced four coverage-shaped figures in one sitting, three of them wrong, and every one was caught the same way — by reading a SAMPLE before believing the COUNT. The same error then appeared a fourth time in the new dangling-target invariant (it flagged 8 phantom danglings that were the anonymous-struct case) and was fixed the same way. A corpus that is not uniformly formatted defeats source-text heuristics, and `zig fmt: off` is exactly the marker that says so.

decisions.wave: 11 - ZIG.GAP.3's headline number was a SYNTACTIC count, and it is 64% method calls
decisions.status: RESTATED at full corpus (wave 15) — the ceiling is ~12,900 sites (4.2%), not ~1,200
decisions.observation: The lane has carried `19,318 qualified-callee sites plus 381 non-local identifier callees per 400 files` as the cross-file `instantiates` remainder for several waves. The count reproduces EXACTLY (19,318 and 63 bare), which is why it was believed. But it counts a SYNTAX — a callee with a dotted head — and says nothing about what the head DENOTES.
decisions.analysis: `zigw-crossfile.ts` builds a real cross-file index (every `@import` binding resolved against the FILESYSTEM, so `../foo.zig` becomes a target rather than a string; every module's exported surface) and then classifies each of the 19,318 by what its base resolves to. 12,332 (63.8%) are method calls through a VALUE chain — `b.build_root.handle.readFileAlloc`, where `b` is a local builder, `.build_root` and `.handle` are its fields and the leaf is a method on a runtime value. Those are not type applications, no cross-file index should resolve them, and the analyzer is right to stay silent. 4,061 (21.0%) are chains rooted at a name this file declares (`std.mem.trim` and the rest — library and in-file calls). 1,180 are rooted at a name the file does not declare (mostly leading-dot enum-literal chains such as `.limited`).
decisions.resolution: Z48's first statement was measured on a 400-FILE draw and is superseded. At the FULL 3,839-file corpus the picture is the same in shape and larger in size: **304,874 qualified callees, of which a cross-file index resolves 8,157 (2.7%)**, plus **4,199** `mod.Type.method` chains that resolve once the type's members are indexed, plus **578** explicit constructions of a type from an imported module. Ceiling **~12,900 sites, 4.2%**. Against that: **190,821 (62.6%)** are method calls through a VALUE chain (`b.build_root.handle.readFileAlloc`) and are not type applications at all; **93,839** are anonymous or type-expression initializers; **57,501** chains are rooted at a type declared in this file; **43,053** at a name the file does not declare. So 95.8% of the population is not an instantiation and never was. The gate that would close the remainder needs the index passed INTO `analyze(root, source, filePath)`, which has no parameter for it — an API question, and now a scoped one with a known ceiling.
decisions.cost: Two of this lane's carried numbers have now turned out to be syntactic counts wearing a semantic label: `219 of 3,839 parse errors` (Z42, actually 93, 43 of them intentional) and `19,318 cross-file sites` (Z48, actually ~1,200). Both were reproduced exactly by the instrument that produced them, and both were meaningless. An exact reproduction is evidence that the COUNT is faithful, and no evidence at all that the CATEGORY is.

decisions.wave: 11 - #963 was filed against a store defect that was already fixed
decisions.status: RESOLVED - 1,485 of 1,485 same-named-container cases are disambiguated by containment; 0 are defects
decisions.observation: This lane reported #963 for several waves as 'the indexer resolves ownership by NAME within a file, so two same-named containers conflate every member', counted 1,485 collisions over 3,000 files, and called the item BLOCKED ON AN OWNER DECISION. All three parts of that were wrong, and the wrongness was checkable in one grep.
decisions.analysis: `parallel-indexer.ts` resolves a symbol's owner with `enclosingStoreableIdByName`, preferring the innermost same-name candidate whose extent COVERS the child's line, with the exact spelling tried before its leaf. It is implemented, not merely commented, and it was measured over ten pinned heavy repos before landing (`zig zig 71,957 / 12,421 / 8,097 / 7,153` in validation/m14/measurements/containment-owner-span-612.json, `zls zig 1,706 / 196 / 24 / 24`). The anchoring data it needs is the container symbols' own ranges, which this analyzer already publishes — so nothing was missing from the analyzer either, and there was no decision left for an owner to make.
decisions.resolution: `zigw-ownership.ts` now resolves ownership the way the store does before counting a collision, and reports the two numbers separately: at 3,000 files / 136,720 symbols / 89,267 owned, AGREE 84,442, PHANTOM_OWN 0, ORPHAN 0, **COLLISION 1,485 — of which enclosure disambiguates 1,485, leaving 0 genuinely ambiguous**.
decisions.cost: The verifier counted AMBIGUITY as UNRESOLVABILITY, which is the same category error as Z48's syntactic count and Z42's error-node definition: a faithful number attached to the wrong question. Three of this lane's largest figures have now turned out to be counts of the right things under the wrong heading — and in this case it produced a filed issue blocking work that was already done.

decisions.wave: 12 - F8 was never bun-only, and Zig was the lane failing it
decisions.status: FIXED - F8 now runs under tsx and reports 8/8 sections pass
decisions.observation: The lane had carried 'F8 corpus/fixture coverage scripts remain bun-only and report filesScanned: 0 on this machine' as a blocked item. Two claims, both wrong. `completeness-inventory.ts` runs unmodified under `npx tsx`, and when it does it reports a FAILURE for zig, not a zero.
decisions.analysis: `zig COMPLETENESS FAIL: 2 node type(s) in NO bucket: ERROR, MISSING` and `FAIL section-a-structural - 98 types, 15 handled, 83 silent, 5 gaps`. The completeness inventory adds the universal `ERROR`/`MISSING` pair to every language's node-type enumeration (completeness-inventory.ts:832-840) because the wasm ABI's `nodeTypeForId` does not list them, and then requires the spec to classify it - F1 and the bash F8 census reuse the same pair, and that comment is explicit that a spec which correctly classifies ERROR 'was being told its own row was grammar drift', with 'the fix is never to delete the correct row'. Zig had no row for either.
decisions.resolution: Both classified `handled_verified`, which is what the analyzer does: real-zig-analyzer.ts:736 handles `node.type === "ERROR" || node.isMissing` and pushes a diagnostic per occurrence with 1-based columns (Z2), deliberately avoiding `node.hasError` because the root spans the file and one parse error cascaded into 163 pipeline rows on aro/Attribute.zig (#897). Result: `zig: 98 types classified; sections A-H: 8/8 pass`.
decisions.cost: An item parked as 'not runnable on this machine' had a real failure sitting behind it. The claim was inherited from a document rather than from a run - the same mechanism as Z43's PHANTOM_OWN 0 and Z45's F1 unknown=0 - and the cost of inheriting a claim about a GATE is that the gate stops being watched. Four of this lane's figures have now turned out to be inherited rather than measured, and every one of them was wrong.

decisions.wave: 14 - the full-corpus run: every gate had only ever seen 200 files
decisions.status: TRUTH BEHIND - fixed; uses/calls is 0/0 over 290,530 agreements at 3,839 files
decisions.observation: Every bidirectional gate in this lane was a 200-FILE draw. The ownership verifier and declaration coverage had run at 3,000 and 3,839, but the relationship gates never had. Running all of them at full corpus found a 410-row class the draw could not reach: symmetric PHANTOM 410 / MISSING 410 on uses and calls.
decisions.analysis: `zig/lib/compiler/aro/aro/Hideset.zig:132` is `pub fn @"union"(self: *Hideset, a: Index, b: Index) !Index` — `union` is a keyword, so the function is declared with a QUOTED identifier.
